current_bottleneck: The bottleneck is objective-level broad-frame conditional path calibration, not another wrapper architecture. 510a and 593a both generate realistic local changes and cross-cell structure but fail the joint future-path law on level location, per-window coverage floors, regime-cell coverage, aggregate kurtosis, and active-cell mean-reversion geometry.
last_result_summary: 595a checked recent time-series work: DistDF/ICLR 2026 argues for joint-distribution Wasserstein alignment because point/direct losses can be biased under label autocorrelation; vLinear/WFMLoss argues final-series-oriented flow objectives can beat velocity-oriented objectives; Sundial/TimeFlow and TSFlow support continuous generative path modeling but do not justify another wrapper; TimePFN suggests synthetic priors for small-data time series but is a larger fallback; MixLinear supports simple efficient temporal/frequency structure but not the immediate probabilistic-law bottleneck.
next_step_recommendation: Run 596 as a clean objective-level experiment: start from 510a final, keep the AR flow architecture unchanged, and finetune the native model with a final-path joint-distribution objective using full-path energy plus sliced/projection Wasserstein terms and a small FM anchor. Evaluate first on the 441-window broad frame. Do not add regime labels, per-cell corrections, low-rank decoders, or separate IV/anchor-factor branches.
current_best_note: 510a/392a remain the historical short-frame best learned IV laws at 8/11, but 594a shows 510a is only 5/11 on the broader 441-window frame. 574a remains the best risk-manager joint stress product. 593a is clean but below same-frame 510a at 4/11, so it is not a replacement.
oracle_feasibility_note: 435a reaches 11/11 only as a validation-future oracle upper bound; it is not a deployable or learned conditional scenario generator.
